# PR #148 correctness review

## A. Verdict

**block** at `5de084c74c75ea63532bec6f4eb36a9f872092d7`.

Two P2 findings in AC1's measurement instrument: some typed HTTP registration refusals are not counted, and native startup/standby attempts are mislabelled. The cheap-refusal brake and retired-address loop shutdown are accepted within the packet's narrowed scope.

## B. Scope

Reviewed the PR-owned delta from merge-base `27efa69ced77776e3a25b990c68aa790c3f518bf` to this full head, including its four non-merge commits. Main's imported changes were not re-reviewed. The detached worktree remained clean and pinned; no product edits or checkout movement.

The packet explicitly defers AC2's live attribution, the unchanged-repeat skip in tk-0004 and the shim optimization in tk-0005. These are not findings. Plan/phase/backpressure AC states remain unchecked; tk-0001/tk-0002 alone are checked. The PR correctly says `Refs #145` and `Delivers: none`, not whole-issue completion.

## C. Acceptance coverage

| Claim | Disposition |
|---|---|
| AC1: bounded attempt counters and ping projection | Enum keys bound path/mode/outcome to at most 180 combinations; seat tallies retain at most 64 named keys plus overflow. A single mutex protects consistent snapshots. Unit tests cover count/ps arithmetic, overflow and unknown client labels; service and HTTP tests cover successful/service-refused attempts. **F001/F002 leave all-attempt and client-path coverage incomplete.** |
| AC3: cheap native refusal | Accepted for the packet's narrower cheap-refusal slice. `explicit_session_conflict` is the same predicate before observation and again under registration exclusion. It only vetoes; it grants nothing and removes no lock-time check. **A brake, not admission policy.** The CI test records zero observations for the foreign-session retired claim and a positive observation control for the recorded session, with the registry unchanged. |
| AC4: terminal retired registration | Accepted for the packet's narrower client-shutdown slice. Only HTTP 400, v2, `ok:false`, `/v1/register`, `E-RS-SEAT-RETIRED` sets the new retired flag. The heartbeat calls the existing idempotent receive hold, aborting both loops; the receive loop already terminates on non-retryable registration errors. CI verifies one registration/one held report, discriminator negative controls and retained healthy lease/backoff behavior. |
| AC2/AC5: live cost attribution | Owed after deploy; not claimed from unit tests or Linux CI. |
| AC6: docs/states | Ping/attempt API documentation present; no new verb needs roster changes. DD validation in CI is explicitly unavailable; completion remains unchecked. |

## D. Findings

**F001, P2: HTTP early refusals bypass the attempt counters.**

`crates/daemon/src/http/mod.rs:949-1006` returns before the only `register_via` call at line 1013 for an invalid seat role, pane-observation errors, a claimed process outside the observed subtree, or a disappeared pane process.

For example, an authenticated, deserializable `/v1/register` request carrying `role:"not-a-seat-role"` and `attempt:"explicit"` returns the typed role refusal immediately. No attempt or per-seat/path/outcome count is recorded: `RegistrationService::count` is reached only after `register_via` settles. A real request and refusal can therefore leave `data.registrations.total` unchanged. This contradicts AC1's every-attempt contract and hides entry-boundary failures from the attribution instrument.

**Repair:** account for every deserialized registration attempt once, including these early refusals/errors, while preserving native claim provenance and avoiding double counting successful/service-refused attempts. Add an HTTP regression with an early refusal plus a counted service-path control, asserting totals and the appropriate path/mode/outcome. The current `first_light` regression exercises a refusal inside the service, not these earlier branches.

**F002, P2: native startup allocation and initial standby retries do not carry their promised path labels.**

At `.copilot/extensions/pij/store.mjs:412-414`, `resolveRegistration` sends a new address's first `/v1/register` through `registerWithPrecedence` without `attempt`; `chooseRegistration` does not add it either. The daemon maps this current client's startup request to `unspecified`, rather than `explicit`. The outer startup loop in `extension.mjs:196-207,230-238` also retries that unlabeled allocation after a holder standby.

Separately, at `store.mjs:1384`, the `!this.reconnectRegistration` branch takes precedence over `standingBy`. When the bridge's first registration is held, `reconnectRegistration` remains unset until a success; after standby the next attempt is still labelled `explicit`, not `lease-retry`. The existing initial-holder standby test exercises this flow but records precedence only, not attempt labels.

These are paths the new current client knows, not intentional support for old clients with no label. Counting startup/standby work as `unspecified` or `explicit` obscures the retry trigger this PR is meant to attribute.

**Repair:** label address allocation as explicit initially and lease-retry after standby, and prioritize the standby reason when a bridge has not yet registered successfully. Add producer-boundary tests for fresh allocation and first-registration hold/standby/retry, checking captured `/v1/register` bodies and their daemon counter keys.

## E. CI evidence

[CI run 42351634792](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42351634792) names this full head; all four jobs passed. Downloaded JUnit contains **2,027 executed cases, zero failures/errors**; the Rust summary separately reports five skipped cases.

Named passing cases include both attempt-count tests, bounded seat overflow, client-label normalization, the zero-observation retired-address guard, ping's registration projection, existing host-ancestor/ps gates and all spawn-site guards. Both Node versions report **2,200 Vitest cases passed, six skipped**, and **323 native-extension cases passed**, including the two new retired-address cases.

The latest body-edited [Delivers run 42352055393](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42352055393) passed at this head. PR state is CLEAN. The green suite does not cover F001's early HTTP refusal totals or F002's initial allocation/standby labels.

## F. Cost and proof limits

No new loop, timer or daemon launch. Counters add an in-process per-attempt tally and bounded-map snapshot on ping. AC3 adds one pre-observation registry lookup for an explicit native address and avoids ancestry reads on a known conflict; the existing lock-time check remains. AC4 removes the retired registration retry loop, otherwise retaining receive/heartbeat lease behavior. No blanket positive identity cache is introduced.

All CI jobs run on Linux. The changed non-Linux ancestry observer's ps-counter closure is source-reviewed, not compiled/executed by this CI receipt. No local build/test or mutation was run under the packet's CI-only instruction. Both Node jobs explicitly report ddocs UNAVAILABLE. Independent security/performance and AC2's live reading remain separately owned.

## G. Commands

Read-only git head/status/merge-base/log/diffs; source, tests and plan/task/backpressure reads; PR and issue metadata; exact-head CI jobs/logs; downloaded JUnit inspection. No local builds/tests, runtime probes, branch writes or product changes.

## H. Handover and harness feedback

Keep this head frozen until a repair round is authorized. Return a new final head with endpoint-refusal accounting and producer-label regressions in CI; retain the accepted brake/shutdown behavior and explicit deferrals.

**magicWand:** make the instrument prove itself at its outer producer boundaries, including a known early refusal and first-standby retry, rather than only manually feeding enum tallies. **difficulty:** all-success CI is not evidence that an attribution counter sees every ingress path.
